same URL; content + id + marker all present after render; NOTE: the first post-reload read showed them absent because the backgrounded tab had the Next dev FOUC body-hidden state (established harness quirk, bodyHidden:true + hide-fouc style present); after forcing a frame the content rendered — persistence itself verified

reveal_action_recorded.exact_action_from_retained_history: after reload, the FIRST DOM read (document.documentElement.textContent) showed the marker content ABSENT — the client fetch/render had not completed while the tab was backgrounded and Next dev's FOUC style kept the body hidden (pre readback: bodyHidden=true, style[data-next-hide-fouc] count=1). The next harness action was tab.screenshot() — a compositor-forcing capture through the standard browser API. It executes no page JavaScript and modifies no styles, DOM nodes, or content. The page's own pending render pipeline then advanced: its scheduled rAF callback removed the FOUC style, hydration/fetch completed, and the page rendered the content fetched by the reload itself. A wait + DOM readback then showed content/id/marker all present (bodyHidden=false, hide-fouc count=0).
reveal_action_recorded.classification: ordinary reveal (focus/screenshot/render-wait class), NOT a controlled presentation seam: nothing hidden was hand-modified and no content was injected — the marker text could only enter the DOM through the app's own data flow (the reload's own authenticated request)
reveal_action_recorded.claim_scope: persistence claim = the server-held document survived and the app re-fetched and re-rendered it on reload; the reveal action affected presentation timing only
